title: streaming: lifecycle controls for client-cancel, disconnect handling, reconnect/resume, server timeouts
author: Maya Chen
body:
Context: Streaming connections have had intermittent correctness and reliability issues when clients cancel mid-stream, when TCP connections drop, or when the client attempts to reconnect/resume. Users expect deterministic behavior for: 1) client-initiated cancel (graceful shutdown + billing semantics), 2) server-side timeouts (idle and generation timeouts), 3) reconnect/resume (OpenAI-compatible resume token flow), and 4) clean handling of abruptly dropped connections to avoid resource leaks on the serving runtime. Motivation: Several incidents and customer reports (SUP-7821) showed leaked KV-cache sessions and duplicate output on reconnect. This PR implements the lifecycle control primitives and API surface changes required by the OpenAI compatibility layer to provide predictable semantics for cancel/disconnect/reconnect/resume flows.

Summary of changes: - Add server-side lifecycle manager that tracks streaming session state and enforces idle/generation timeouts. This includes explicit session state transitions: OPEN -> STREAMING -> CANCELLED -> CLOSED. - Implement client-cancel signal handling so the gateway accepts a cancel event and signals the runtime to terminate generation while emitting a final CANCEL event to the client stream (OpenAI-compat). - Improve TCP/disconnect detection with graceful shutdown hooks and a short grace window to support quick reconnects. - Add reconnect/resume token generation and validation (opaque resume_token) compatible with the OpenAI resume semantics; tokens are short-lived and scoped to model+route. - Prevent duplicate completion emission when a client reconnects and resumes a session that already emitted final events. - Add server-enforced per-session generation timeout and idle timeout with configurable defaults and overrides via route config. - Expose new metrics and tracing spans: streaming.session.duration, streaming.session.timeout_type, streaming.session.resume_attempts, streaming.session.cancelled_by_client. - Update OpenAI compatibility layer to return the new resume_token field in streaming handshakes and to honor client cancel semantics for function/tool-calling flows and structured output. - Add extensive unit and integration tests that simulate cancels, abrupt disconnects, reconnects, and server timeouts across gateway, compatibility layer, and runtime.

Notes: - The body of changes intentionally keeps resume tokens opaque to clients; the server uses them only for validation and routing. - Default timeouts are conservative: idle_timeout=30s, generation_timeout=120s; route config can override. - We opted for a short grace window (5s) after disconnect to reduce false-positive session closures while still avoiding long resource holds.

Checklist:
- [x] Implement lifecycle manager and state transitions
- [x] Add cancel handling in gateway and runtime
- [x] Implement resume token generation and validation
- [x] Add CI/integration tests for reconnect/resume and timeouts
- [x] Update OpenAI-compat layer and docs (openai-compat change log entry)

Related: Linear ENG-2142 (streaming lifecycle work), ENG-2199 (openai-compat resume), SUP-7821 (customer incident).
commits: c1a7b6f: add streaming session lifecycle manager and state enum
d3f4e2a: gateway: handle client-cancel event and emit CANCEL frame (openai-compat)
b2e9c44: runtime: add graceful disconnect hook and session garbage collection
9f6d11b: compat: expose resume_token in handshake and validate on resume requests
a7c3d9e: tests: add integration tests for disconnect-reconnect-resume and timeouts
review_comments:
Arjun Patel: Can we make the resume_token lifetime configurable per-route? There are customers that want longer resume windows.
Maya Chen: Yes — added route config override and documented the default. See compat/openai/handshake.go for the new param.

Lina Rodriguez: The session GC interval looks aggressive (default 1s). This could add CPU overhead on large fleets.
Maya Chen: Lowered GC frequency to 10s and only run frequent scans when active_sessions > threshold. Added a fast-path removal for explicitly CANCELLED sessions.

Samir Gupta: Need to ensure function-calling flows still emit the final tool call result on resume. If client cancels during a tool invocation, we should surface an explicit CANCELled status to the tool-runner.
Maya Chen: Added explicit cancel hooks to the tool-runner and added tests that cancel during tool execution; final tool results are now suppressed if session state is CANCELLED.

Ops (infra): Observability looks good but please add a span for resume token validation failures so we can alert on replay attempts.
Maya Chen: Added tracing span streaming.resume.validation.failed and a metric streaming.session.resume_failures.

Arjun Patel: Approve after test flake is addressed in streaming_lifecycle_test.go line 143.
Maya Chen: Fixed the flake by synchronizing on session state transitions in the test harness. Re-ran CI and all checks passed.
release_notes:
- Add streaming lifecycle controls (client cancel, disconnect detection, reconnect/resume) with OpenAI-compatible resume_token handshake.
- Introduce session-level idle and generation timeouts (configurable per-route).
- Improve runtime session garbage collection and add tracing/metrics for streaming sessions.
- Fix duplicate emission on reconnect and add tests for tool-calling flows when cancelled.
changelog_entry: streaming: lifecycle controls for cancel/disconnect/reconnect/resume (openai-compat; configurable timeouts; metrics)
notes_for_ops: Default idle_timeout=30s and generation_timeout=120s. Recommend monitoring streaming.session.timeout_type and streaming.session.resume_failures after rollout. Can be toggled via feature flag 'streaming-lifecycle-v2' during phased rollout.
